title: Design the Backend for a Flash Sale
description: Scale a stateless request tier behind a load balancer to carry a 1,000,000 req/s flash sale while keeping every server within an 80% capacity headroom budget.

prompt.text:
You are the backend architect for an e-commerce website called **QuickCart**.

QuickCart is running a major flash sale. During the sale, the website is expected to receive up to **1,000,000 requests per second**.

Each backend server can handle a maximum of **100,000 requests per second**. To keep the servers stable, you should use a maximum of **80% of their capacity**.

The Load Balancer is already configured and can distribute incoming requests evenly across all the servers you add.

Drag and drop the required components to build the backend architecture for QuickCart.
functionalRequirements: Accept incoming user traffic at the load balancer
Distribute traffic evenly across a pool of backend servers
Serve the full offered load without dropping requests

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Serve the full 1,000,000 req/s offered load
Drop no requests under peak load

structuralRules.description: The design must include a load balancer.

dryRunCase.description: Representative peak load the student may dry-run against.

cases.description: 1,000,000 req/s peak with the 80% headroom rule enforced.

invariants.description: No server may exceed 80% of its capacity during the sale.

checks.description: Includes a pool of backend servers
Serves peak load without dropping requests
Every server stays within the 80% capacity headroom budget
